input.original_instruction: We are starting out outside beside a pool but we are going to turn around going inside the house. The pool and the grass will be on your right. Then when we turn to go in we will go beside the black table and then turn left. Going between the white curtain and the couch. We will continue going forward to  where we are now going back outside through a different exit. We will walk through the patio furniture, keeping the coffee table on the left hand side. When we are at the far side of the patio with a pillar in front of us and the poolway stuff to the left. You have reached your destination.

decision.rationale: The instruction is kept as one coherent executable route because no useful, independently closed boundary is supported without detaching a coupled maneuver.

teaching_notes.why_this_case_matters: KEEP example: the instruction forms one coherent local route objective (We are starting out outside beside a pool but we are going to turn around going inside the…). The apparent action clauses do not establish a separate completed target with a useful, source-supported handoff.
teaching_notes.reusable_rule: Keep the instruction as one stage when its turns, traversal and target selection form one coupled maneuver and no independent intermediate completion point is stated. Preserve all action order and conditions in the same stage.
teaching_notes.executable_reuse_test: For every stage, verify entry state, complete ordered process, target, supported completion event or final goal directive, and scoped conditions. For every cut, verify the preceding exit and next entry can be connected without teleportation or an invented stop.
teaching_notes.anti_pattern: Do not split merely because the source contains multiple verbs or sentences; do not invent an intermediate stop or endpoint.
teaching_notes.retrieval_rule: Retrieve for short or tightly coupled routes where splitting at a turn, pass-by cue or descriptive observation would create an orientation-only stage without an independent navigation target.
